1. δ 1.43 (d, 3H) - A doublet representing a methyl group
2. δ 2.69 (s, 6H) - A singlet representing two equivalent methyl groups (N(CH3)2)
3. δ 5.05 (q, 1H) - A quartet representing one proton
4. δ 7.13 (ddd, 1H) - An aromatic proton
5. δ 7.39 (ddd, 2H) - Two equivalent aromatic protons
6. δ 7.90 (ddd, 1H) - An aromatic proton

Counting the different chemical environments:
1. One type of methyl group (δ 1.43)
2. One type of N(CH3)2 protons (δ 2.69)
3. One type of CH proton (δ 5.05)
4. Three different types of aromatic protons (δ 7.13, 7.39, and 7.90)

In total, there are 6 different types of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms.
